README: PROVENANCE. Which version of _skeleton this tree came from, and when. It is the only thing that makes the question 'which of the 67 tools has the fixed packager?' answerable at all — without it, the answer requires reading 1,600 lines of inherited test code per tool and guessing which differences were deliberate. TEMPLATE.md step 0 tells you to stamp `tool` and `copiedAt` the moment you copy the folder; `node tools/audit-fleet.mjs` reads this file in every tool and reports what has drifted.

NOTES.skeletonVersion: set by the SKELETON, not by you. Never edit it in a tool: it records which version you copied FROM, which is exactly the fact the fleet audit needs. It is bumped in _skeleton itself, and CHANGELOG-skeleton.md says what changed.
NOTES.tool: your tool's folder name. Empty here because _skeleton is not a tool.
NOTES.copiedAt: an ISO date, the day you copied the folder. Empty here for the same reason.
NOTES.inherited: The files below are the ones a tool is expected NOT to edit — they are the shared substrate, and the fleet audit compares their content against the current skeleton. Editing one is allowed; it just has to be a decision somebody can see, rather than 67 copies quietly diverging.
